title: PowerToys Monaco Preview Handler displays UTF-16LE .reg files with NUL characters

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a minimal UTF-16LE .reg repro, confirmed the bug on 0.101.2362.0, and current Monaco preview code re-encodes decoded text with the original file encoding before handing it to HTML that always decodes the base64 bytes as UTF-8-style text.
evidence: Minimal.reg visibly contains UTF-16LE NUL bytes between characters.
The reporter confirmed the issue still reproduces on 0.101.2362.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the UTF-8 normalization design and add a UTF-16LE regression test.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the Monaco preview encoding mismatch between the C# producer and JavaScript bootstrapper.

issue_context.summary: Monaco Preview Handler successfully reads the UTF-16LE file into managed text, but then re-serializes that text back into UTF-16LE bytes even though the Monaco HTML bootstrap always decodes the payload as UTF-8-style text.
known_information: A minimal UTF-16LE .reg repro ZIP is attached.
The built-in Windows text preview handler renders the same file correctly.
The reporter manually updated to 0.101.2362.0 and confirmed the issue still reproduces there.
inferences: The bug is in Monaco’s preview transport layer, not in Registry Editor or the Windows preview pane.
Any UTF-16 text path using the same bootstrap is at risk, not only .reg files.
issue_context.analysis: This is the clearest implementation-grade design candidate in the batch because the attachment, managed preview control, and JavaScript bootstrapper all show the same mismatch.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body, reporter follow-up, and both attached ZIP files.
Confirmed the repro attachment contains UTF-16LE NUL bytes and the workaround ZIP only restores the built-in Windows text preview handler.
Reviewed MonacoPreviewHandlerControl.cs and src/Monaco/index.html end to end.

comment.body: Approve the UTF-8 normalization design for Monaco Preview Handler issue 50138.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize Monaco preview text to UTF-8 before injecting into index.html
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The preview control decodes UTF-16LE .reg files into a .NET string, then turns that string back into UTF-16LE bytes and embeds them into HTML that always interprets the base64 payload as UTF-8-style text.
plan: Keep detected encoding only for reading the source file into a .NET string.
Serialize the resulting text to UTF-8 bytes when populating [[PT_CODE]], or teach the browser bootstrap to decode an explicit matching encoding.
Add a regression test for a UTF-16LE .reg preview.
verification: Preview the attached UTF-16LE Minimal.reg file and confirm Monaco shows plain text without red NUL squares.
Preview a UTF-8 version of the same file and confirm current behavior stays intact.

confidence.rationale: The attachment, current source, and Monaco HTML bootstrap path all line up on one encoding mismatch.

design.root_cause: MonacoPreviewHandlerControl reads the file with the detected encoding, but then serializes the resulting .NET string back into the original encoding when building [[PT_CODE]]. src/Monaco/index.html always decodes the base64 payload as UTF-8-style text, so UTF-16LE files surface their interleaved NUL bytes in the browser preview.
evidence: [Observed] The attached Minimal.reg file is UTF-16LE and contains NUL bytes between characters.
[Observed] The reporter confirmed the bug on 0.101.2362.0 and the built-in Windows preview handler renders the same file correctly.

affected_files.purpose: Reads the source file and serializes it into the HTML bootstrap payload.
Bootstraps Monaco and decodes the injected base64 payload into editor text.
Natural location for a UTF-16LE Monaco preview regression test.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The method reads the file into a managed string, then base64-encodes encodingToUse.GetBytes(fileContent).
implementation_steps.change: Keep the detected encoding only for reading the file. Serialize the already-decoded text to UTF-8 bytes before populating [[PT_CODE]], or pass explicit encoding metadata so producer and consumer agree.
edge_cases: Do not break UTF-8 files that already preview correctly.
Keep formatter output on the same normalized text path.
Preserve large-file handling and current settings flags.
tests: Preview a UTF-16LE .reg fixture and assert the rendered header has no NUL placeholders.
Preview an existing UTF-8 source fixture and confirm unchanged rendering.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The browser bootstrap always converts the base64 payload with decodeURIComponent(atob(...)), which assumes UTF-8-style bytes.
implementation_steps.change: Either keep the bootstrap as-is and rely on UTF-8 producer bytes, or replace the decode block with an explicit TextDecoder-based path that documents the canonical payload encoding.
implementation_steps.code_block:
var bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(base64code), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
var code = new TextDecoder("utf-8").decode(bytes);
edge_cases: Keep compatibility with the WebView2 runtime used by preview handlers.
tests: Confirm the Monaco page still renders UTF-8 fixtures correctly.
Verify the UTF-16LE .reg fixture no longer renders NUL boxes.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: UI coverage validates Monaco preview in general, but no regression test covers UTF-16LE text passed through the Monaco bootstrap.
implementation_steps.change: Add a UTF-16LE .reg fixture and extend Monaco preview coverage so the test asserts readable registry-header text instead of NUL-separated output.
edge_cases: Keep the fixture small and deterministic.
Prefer an assertion that still exercises the full preview bootstrap path.
tests: Run the targeted Monaco preview UI test with the new UTF-16LE fixture.
Keep the existing Monaco syntax-highlight test green.

verify: Build PowerToys with the existing tools\build\build.cmd workflow so the Monaco preview handler and PreviewPane.UITests project are rebuilt together.
Run the targeted PreviewPane.UITests Monaco coverage with vstest.console.exe after locating the built PreviewPane.UITests.dll.
In Explorer, preview the attached UTF-16LE Minimal.reg file and confirm the Monaco preview shows readable text with no NUL squares.
Preview a UTF-8 file and confirm existing Monaco behavior is unchanged.
risks: Changing the producer/consumer encoding contract could regress other non-UTF-8 files if only one side is updated.
A fixture-only test that does not exercise the HTML bootstrap would miss this failure mode.
alternatives: Keeping producer bytes in the original encoding and teaching index.html to decode multiple formats adds unnecessary complexity for a path that already holds normalized managed text.
Switching .reg files back to the built-in Windows handler avoids the symptom but does not fix Monaco preview for other UTF-16 text files.

design_decision.reason: Exactly one issue was expanded to a full implementation-grade design in this batch.

confidence.rationale: Repro attachment and source point at one concrete encoding mismatch.

adversarial_review.conclusion: No blocking objection: the producer emits UTF-16LE bytes while the browser bootstrap decodes UTF-8-style bytes.
non_blocking_notes: Keep the regression test end to end.
